traits.note: Drilled, physical, direct - the Crazy Gang punched far above the squad
The Galácticos side that actually won something. Makélélé did the work that made the rest of it possible, which is exactly why selling him broke it.
Zidanes y Pavones, without Makélélé. Four of the best attacking players alive and nobody to win the ball back — the cohesion is the story of the season.

Ancelotti's Christmas tree, and the oldest side in Europe: Maldini and Costacurta either side of forty, Pirlo dictating, Kaká and Seedorf tucked behind the striker. Narrow by design, which is what the centre focus says.
Mancini’s side won seventeen league games in a row. Control through Cambiasso and Vieira, and the attack tilted right where Maicon and Figo were.
Spalletti’s strikerless experiment. Totti dropped off as a false nine and scored 26; everything went through the middle, which is what the centre focus says.
Pellegrini’s 96 points won nothing because Barcelona took 99. Ronaldo and Higuaín scored 53 between them in the league; the whole side tilted left towards Ronaldo and Marcelo.
99 points, and the only squad in the database that can actually execute tiki-taka: Xavi, Iniesta and Busquets in midfield with Piqué behind them. Messi scored 34.
Built down the right touchline. Jesús Navas ran the line every week and crossed for two forwards who could both attack it.
Broke and sold half the team, then finished third anyway. Villa, Silva and Mata was as good a front three as anyone outside the top two had.
Robben right, Ribéry left, Gómez attacking everything in the middle. Lost the final at home and won nothing; the same plan won the treble a year later.
Klopp’s double, and 81 points — a Bundesliga record at the time. The whole side was built to win the ball back in the opposition half and go immediately.
The treble. 91 points from 34 games, the title won in March, and Ribéry’s best season. Martínez was signed to press, and it is the difference from the year before.
Beaten at Wembley by Bayern, having put four past Real Madrid on the way. Reus and Götze either side of Lewandowski was the best young attack in Europe.
102 points, still the Serie A record. Conte’s 3-5-2 with the BBC behind Pirlo, and all the width coming from wing-backs.
Allegri won the league after taking three points from the first five games. Twenty conceded all season; the plan was to keep it tight and let Dybala settle it.
Sarri’s first great side, and the most rehearsed team in Italy — the same eleven, the same patterns, every week. Higuaín scored 36, which is still the Serie A record.
The most drilled side in the league, and the squad matches it exactly: the highest press resistance and creation in the division. Set pieces are a weapon in their own right.
Genuine pace and almost no press resistance, so building from the back is not available to them. Better on the break than in possession, which the results bore out.

Committed to controlling games with a squad that presses far better than it resists a press — the second-highest pressing quality in the league and almost the lowest press resistance. Enormous individual talent, very little settled understanding.
Control rather than chaos. Elite on the ball and creative, but this iteration presses far less than the peak side, so possession fits it better than positional play.
Wins it back high and fast. The one squad with both the pressing and the pace to do it, and the press resistance to play through a press in return.
The quickest squad in the league behind a very high line. Thrilling and repeatedly punished, which is what a high line without recovery cover buys you.
Aggressive rather than intricate. Presses hard without the technical base to build from the back.
Emery organises a mid-block and attacks the space behind it. Real pace up front; less cover at the back than the plan wants.
Iraola coached the most demanding press in the division. The squad is built for it and for little else.
Not route one — that is a long ball to a target man. Brentford go forward fast and vertically, and their set pieces do the rest. Short of out-and-out runners for it, which is the honest limitation.
A coherent identity that survives manager changes. Comfortable on the ball, short of a genuine chance creator.
Glasner drilled the wing-back system to break at pace. Width on both flanks is the whole plan.
The slowest squad in the division by a distance and among the most aerial. Deep, compact, and genuinely dangerous from a dead ball — the shape the players actually suit.
Organised, mid-block, no strong bias in any direction. Balanced asks nothing of a squad, which is what makes it the safe answer rather than the weak one.
McKenna got a promoted squad pressing aggressively. Overmatched rather than disorganised, and the fit shows the gap between the plan and the players.
An excellent low block that broke at speed, with genuine aerial strength to survive the siege. Results ran well ahead of the squad on paper.

The clearest case in the league of a side committed to a style it could not execute: bottom-three press resistance, negative creation, and a manager insistent on playing out from the back. The fit penalty is the point, not a bug.
The most aerial squad in the division and the slowest, with negative recovery pace. Sitting deep is not a choice so much as the only thing this group can do.
Fast wing-backs and little control in between. The attack lives in the wide areas and on the break.
Bilardo built a functional, hard-working side and pointed it at one player. Everything came through the middle because everything came through Maradona.
The scudetto dei record: 58 points from 34 games under Trapattoni. Compact, ruthless on the break, and carried by two Germans — Matthäus driving through the middle and Brehme’s left foot.
Scolari’s 3-5-2, with Cafú and Roberto Carlos providing every yard of width and the three R’s in front of them. Ronaldo scored eight and won the tournament.
